title: Cappadocia, Turkey
body:
Up before 5am most days to catch the balloon launches from the valley
floor. The rock formations look completely different depending on which
side the light's coming from — spent a lot of time just repositioning.

title: Dolomites, Italy
body:
Four days hiking between rifugios with just enough gear to keep it light.
The enrosadira — the way the peaks turn pink at sunset — is the reason
everyone says to come here, and it's the reason.

title: Havana, Cuba
body:
Shot on foot through Centro Habana and along the Malecón at golden hour,
when the sea spray catches the light. Color came easy here — the hard
part was keeping the gear dry.

title: Hoi An, Vietnam
body:
Timed the trip around the lantern festival on the river. Shot the old
town mostly at blue hour, right when the paper lanterns start to
outshine the streetlights.

title: Kurdistan
body:
A season based out of Erbil, working outward into the surrounding
villages and the citadel old town. Kurdistan isn't a single point on a
map, so this pin marks the base the work was shot from rather than the
whole region.

title: Kyoto, Japan
body:
Autumn in Kyoto. Three weeks following the color of the maples through
Arashiyama and the backstreets of Gion, shooting mostly at dawn before the
crowds arrived. The light through the bamboo groves ended up being the
whole story.

title: Lofoten, Norway
body:
Midnight sun shooting — meant entire days with no real darkness to plan
around. Mostly fishing villages and the mountains dropping straight into
the fjords. Slept badly, shot well.

title: Marrakech, Morocco
body:
A week in the medina shooting mostly handheld and wide. The light in
Jemaa el-Fnaa changes completely between noon and dusk — ended up going
back to the same square four evenings in a row to get the smoke and the
crowd right.

title: Namib Desert, Namibia
body:
Climbed the dunes at Sossusvlei before sunrise to get the ridge lines
while the sand was still cool. The contrast between the red dunes and
the dead white clay pan at Deadvlei did most of the work for me.

title: Oaxaca, Mexico
body:
Covered Día de los Muertos for most of this set — markets, altars, and
the cemetery vigils at Xoxocotlán. Loud, bright, and completely unlike
how it gets described secondhand.

title: Patagonia, Chile
body:
Six days in Torres del Paine waiting out weather that changes every twenty
minutes. The wind made the tripod useless half the time, so most of this
set ended up handheld. Worth it for the one morning the towers cleared.

title: Reykjavik, Iceland
body:
Ten days chasing aurora forecasts that kept lying. Spent most nights on
black-sand coastlines west of the city, waiting out clouds. Got maybe
forty minutes of real sky across the whole trip — made every one of them
count.

title: Varanasi, India
body:
Five mornings on the ghats starting before sunrise. The light off the
Ganges does something to color temperature I haven't seen anywhere else.
Shot almost entirely from a rented boat to stay out of the way.
